claims.claim: 1872, Fogg lives at Saville Row, member of the Reform Club
claims.evidence: 'Mr. Phileas Fogg lived, in 1872, at No. 7, Saville Row'; 'Reform Club, an imposing edifice in Pall Mall'
'whatever he did was so exactly the same thing'; 'exactly at midnight'

claims.claim: Hires French servant Passepartout the same day
claims.evidence: 'On this very 2nd of October he had dismissed James Forster'; 'a Frenchman, named Passepartout'

claims.claim: That evening bets club friends he can go around the world in 80 days
claims.evidence: 'This very evening?' 'This very evening,' returned Phileas Fogg; 'twenty thousand pounds'
'twenty thousand pounds against anyone who wishes'
'Bring down my mackintosh and traveling-cloak'; train leaves (twenty minutes before nine)

claims.claim: Fix thinks Fogg a bank robber
claims.evidence: 'I've found the bank robber, Phileas Fogg. Send without delay warrant'

claims.claim: In India they rescue Aouda from a funeral pyre
claims.evidence: 'A suttee'; Passepartout takes the place of the dead rajah; Aouda carried off

claims.claim: Fogg arrested in England by Fix
claims.evidence: 'I arrest you in the Queen's name!' at the Liverpool quay

claims.claim: Reaches London five minutes late and thinks he is ruined
claims.evidence: 'all the clocks in London were striking ten minutes before nine...behind-hand five minutes. He had lost the wager!'

claims.claim: He marries Aouda; then Passepartout finds it is still Saturday
claims.evidence: wedding set for next day; Passepartout: 'Because to-morrow—is Sunday!' 'to-day is Saturday'; 'the marriage took place forty-eight hours after'
claims.fix: He proposes to Aouda; then Passepartout, sent to arrange the wedding, finds it is still Saturday; marries two days later

claims.claim: They gained a day travelling east
claims.evidence: 'In journeying eastward he had gone towards the sun, and the days therefore...'

claims.claim: Fogg dashes to the club and wins
claims.evidence: 'Here I am, gentlemen!'; 'Phileas Fogg had won his wager of twenty thousand pounds!'

claims.claim: Bombay: Passepartout enters temple in his shoes
claims.evidence: pagoda on Malabar Hill; 'went in without first leaving their shoes'; beaten, 'shoeless'

claims.claim: Sir Francis Cromarty British officer in India
claims.evidence: 'Sir Francis Cromarty, one of Mr. Fogg's whist partners'; the general / brigadier

claims.claim: Andrew Stuart club member who bets with Fogg
claims.evidence: 'Andrew Stuart, an engineer' whist; 'This very evening?' asked Stuart
